candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: apply knowledge of medication therapeutic effects, evaluate response to therapy, and provide medication education.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — statin intensity and therapeutic response
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret statin intensity as the expected percentage reduction in LDL-C and recognize that high-intensity therapy targets at least a 50% reduction while individual response must be confirmed with follow-up lipid testing.

options.A: The statin regimen is expected to reduce LDL-C by at least 50%, although the actual response varies among patients and should be assessed with follow-up lipid testing.
options.B: The medication must be administered more frequently than moderate-intensity statins regardless of the specific drug.
options.C: The term refers primarily to medication cost rather than expected lipid lowering.
options.D: The classification guarantees that every client will reach the same absolute LDL-C value after treatment.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ACC/AHA multisociety dyslipidemia guideline classifies statin intensity by expected percentage LDL-C reduction: high-intensity therapy is expected to lower LDL-C by at least 50%, moderate-intensity by 30%–49%, and low-intensity by less than 30%. The guideline also emphasizes that actual percentage reduction varies in clinical practice and follow-up LDL-C assessment is needed to evaluate adherence and treatment effect. B and C misstate the classification. D turns an expected relative effect into a guaranteed identical absolute result.
candidate.source_claim_supported: High-intensity statin therapy is defined by an expected LDL-C reduction of at least 50%, but individual response varies and should be assessed rather than assumed.
candidate.source_document_title: 2026 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
candidate.source_locator: Section 4.2.1.1 Statins, Synopsis and Table 6: statins are categorized by expected percent LDL-C reduction; high-intensity ≥50%, moderate-intensity 30%–49%, low-intensity <30%. The synopsis notes that magnitude of LDL-C lowering varies with patient population and adherence; follow-up LDL-C testing is used to assess adequacy of response and adherence.
candidate.source_organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association and partner societies
candidate.stem: A client is prescribed a high-intensity statin. What does the term 'high-intensity' mean in current dyslipidemia guidance?
